html:
The Kingdom of Sardinia was the state of the House of Savoy, ruled from Turin, that grew into modern Italy. It joined the island of Sardinia to Savoy and Piedmont on the mainland, which is why it is also called Sardinia-Piedmont. The dukes of Savoy gained the island and the royal title in 1720.

In the wars with revolutionary France it lost Savoy and Nice, and from 1802 Piedmont was annexed to France. The king held on only on the island. In 1815 he got his mainland back, plus the old Republic of Genoa and its port.

After 1848 Sardinia was the one Italian state with a constitution and a parliament. Its prime minister Cavour sent troops to the Crimean War to win friends, then allied with France against Austria. The war of 1859 won Lombardy; Savoy and Nice were ceded to France as payment. In 1860 Garibaldi took Sicily and Naples and handed them over. In 1861 the kingdom took a new name, the Kingdom of Italy.
